items.title: Taste cannot be delegated
items.excerpt: An argument that as AI makes everyone a 'creator', taste and editorial judgment become the scarce design skill that can't be handed to a model — and that 'design by committee' dies precisely because someone still has to own the call. A design-leadership lens on where humans stay decisive in an AI workflow.

items.title: The interface has left the building
items.excerpt: How chat, voice, and agentic AI are rewriting the first principles of UX — as the screen stops being the primary surface, designers have to rethink flows, affordances, and control for interfaces that are generated and negotiated at runtime rather than laid out in advance.

items.title: Craft still matters, but it's about outcomes
items.excerpt: AI has moved craft from production to judgment; the same tools can help protect quality if you write your standards down and keep humans reviewing. A practical take on encoding design standards so AI output stays on-brand and on-bar rather than drifting toward generic.

items.title: Design the Moment an AI Agent Needs Human Input
items.excerpt: A recovery-first interaction model for long-running AI tasks: how to design the handoff points — interruptions, approvals, expiring decisions, safe resume — where an autonomous agent must pause for a human. Concrete UX patterns for agentic products. (Lower-authority individual post; include only if a stronger agentic-UX item is missing.)
